source.title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization

accepted.question_text: For nonsmooth regularized optimization problems of the form minimize f(x) + h(x), where f is continuously differentiable and h is proper, lower semicontinuous, and may be nonconvex, can the convergence analysis of the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method be generalized to allow unbounded Hessian or quasi-Newton approximations when those approximations do not deteriorate too fast?

evidence.quote: Hessian approximations are unbounded, provided they do not deteriorate too fast
It may be possible to generalize our analysis along similar lines.

accepted.question_text: For the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method and its related quadratic regularization variant for nonsmooth regularized optimization, can one develop implementations and convergence or complexity analyses that remain valid when function values, gradients, and proximal-operator evaluations are computed inexactly rather than exactly?

evidence.quote: inexact function, gradient, and proximal operator evaluations

accepted.question_text: Can the convergence and worst-case iteration-complexity results established for proximal quasi-Newton trust-region and quadratic-regularization methods in nonsmooth regularized optimization be extended to cubic regularization variants?

evidence.quote: extensions of our results to cubic regularization

accepted.question_text: Can the convergence and complexity results for the nonsmooth regularized trust-region framework be extended to more general nonlinear stepsize-control methods?

evidence.quote: more general nonlinear stepsize control-type methods
